content.thinking: This looks like silent data corruption rather than just a bad deployment — the removed maintenance of total_this_month means stored totals are wrong and metrics stay flat, and reverting the change would only stop further drift, not fix what's already been written incorrectly. So I'll classify silent-data-corruption as the primary issue, with bad-deployment as secondary.

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: The deployment of 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2 at 2026-10-19T09:13:00Z changed record_purchase so it no longer updates the per-account month total (total_this_month_cents). Shopper totals written since then have not matched the purchases behind them. The service itself kept serving normally: metrics are flat and the rollout converged.

supporting_evidence.claim: modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py: removed total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase ('The month is no longer carried')
240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile; oldest affected purchase recorded 2026-10-19T09:14:00Z, one minute after the deploy
All metrics are flat across the window (error_rate, latency, cpu_limit_cores 3.0 constant)
Deployment has converged: all 3 replicas run 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: A code change shipped in revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2 dropped the month-total maintenance from the purchase ledger, which left the shopper totals wrong. The rollout converged, so this is not a version split.

supporting_evidence.claim: modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py: record_purchase no longer carries total_this_month_cents
